main_text.p: lum excedentem, qui & illos quan-doque infestat, vi exorbitantis effer-vescentiæ ab humoribus contrariâ crimoniâ præditis esse productum, deoque calorem naturalem vi natura-lis effervescentiæ in humano corpore exoriri,& propterea Medico calorem, & eadem est frigoris ratio, in corpore humano non considerandum ut quali-tatem primam, ut vulgò putatur; sed ut secundam, utpote ab effervescentia crium in corpore existentium depen-dentem. Hinc seriò monet unus omnium Medicorum præstantissi-mus; l. c. Text. XLII. Oportere Me-dicum potentias humorum, & quid sin-gguli ipsorum in homine facere possunt, perspectum habere: uti & quam affini-tatem humores inter sese habeant, an vi-delicet dulcis humor in aliam speciem mutetur, non à contemperamento, sed ipse desciscens & immutatus ab eo qualis primùm fuerat. amarus aut salsus aut acerbus aut acidus ( sit sanè acidus )

page.notes: Page is partly cut off at the left edge; the first words of each line are damaged and reconstructed only where legible. Some words in the italic passage are doubtful, including "sin-gguli" which is probably a printing error for "sin-guli", and "ipse" which is uncertain. Left-margin letters are cut off by the scan edge.
